key_insight: AI-generated hospital handoffs matched clinician handoffs on overall quality, but traded better organization and completeness for lower conciseness and accuracy.
clinical_relevance: AI may reduce documentation burden for hospitalists, but handoff tools need careful oversight because small differences in error type could affect patient safety.
method: Retrospective comparison of AI-generated vs clinician-authored end-of-rotation handoffs
AI tool used a large language model with clinical notes and EHR data as input
Structured review assessed quality and safety domains
evidence_signal: Overall quality scores were similar (3.7 vs 3.5, p=0.57), with AI scoring higher on organization and completeness but lower on conciseness and accuracy.
watch_item: Retrospective review in a limited workflow may not capture real-world safety risks, and AI handoffs showed some inaccuracies and hallucinations.
paper_title: Quality and Safety profiles of AI-Generated vs Clinician-Generated Handoffs in Hospital Medicine
